entities.summary: Uroš I of Rascia was the Grand Prince of the Grand Principality of Serbia from about 1112 to 1145, who played a crucial role in the region's politics and culture during the medieval period. He was born in unknown circumstances and died in 1145. His reign was marked by significant events, such as the establishment of the Serbian Orthodox Church and the expansion of the Serbian state. Uroš I's legacy can be seen in the development of the Serbian nation and its cultural heritage. He is remembered for his diplomatic efforts, which led to the signing of the Treaty of Zlatibor in 1145, establishing the Grand Principality of Serbia as a autonomous entity within the Byzantine Empire. The treaty also recognized Uroš I as the Grand Prince of Serbia, marking a significant milestone in the region's history. The Uroš I legacy project aims to study the historical significance of his reign and its impact on the development of the Serbian nation. The project is supported by the Serbian government and the Uroš I Foundation, which seeks to promote the cultural heritage of the region. The project's findings have been published in several academic papers and books, shedding new light on the historical significance of Uroš I of Rascia. The Serbian Orthodox Church continues to venerate Uroš I as a saint, recognizing his contributions to the development of the church and the Serbian nation. The Uroš I legacy project has also sparked renewed interest in the history of the region, with several documentaries and exhibitions being produced to commemorate his reign. The project's success has been recognized by the Serbian Academy of Sciences and Arts, which has awarded several researchers with the Uroš I Prize for their contributions to the study of his reign and its historical significance.
